look_here_first: Start with leaf arrangement and head type: alternate, resinous/gland-dotted, usually petiolate leaves below a rounded cluster of many tiny pink-purple heads with no ray florets.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays natural Purola flora and Travis herbarium are firm; a third exact target county was not locked without inference.

best_field_traits: alternate simple elliptic to oblong/lanceolate leaves
leaves usually visibly petiolate and resinous/gland-dotted
rounded/corymbiform mass of many tiny pink-purple heads
heads are discoid with no ray florets
crushed foliage may smell camphor-like but odor is only secondary
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Elliptic to oblong/lanceolate, serrate, generally petiolate, resinous/gland-dotted.
morphology_keys.heads: Small pink-purple discoid heads, no rays.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Heterotheca subaxillaris is also called camphorweed but has conspicuous yellow ray florets. Conoclinium has opposite triangular 3-veined leaves.
